source_refs.note: Book p. 10-12: 1.5.2 (i) graph of sinh x with value table and Figure 1.8, (ii) graph of cosh x with value table and Figure 1.9

blocks.text: Pichle page par hum ne \(\sinh x\) aur \(\cosh x\) ki definitions dekhi thin. Ab sawal yeh hai ke in ke graphs kaise dikhte hain. Graph banane ka hamara pakka tareeqa yeh hai: pehle domain dekho, phir dekho ke \(x\) bohat bara ya bohat chhota hone par function kya karta hai, phir ek khaas point (jaise \(x = 0\)) nikalo, aur aakhir mein values ka table bana kar points jor do. Kitab bhi yahi karti hai.
(i) Graph of sinh x

Hum jaante hain ke \(\sinh x = \frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}\). Ise is tarah bhi likh sakte hain:
\[\sinh x = \dfrac{e^{x} - \frac{1}{e^{x}}}{2} = \dfrac{e^{x} - \left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}}{2}\]

Kyun ke \(e^{x}\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}\) dono ka domain \(\mathbb{R}\) hai, is liye \(\sinh x\) ka domain bhi \(\mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\) hai. Matlab \(x\) ki jagah koi bhi real number rakh sakte hain.

Jab \(x \to \infty\) (yani \(x\) bohat bara hota jaye), to \(e^{x} \to \infty\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x} \to 0\). Is liye \(\sinh x = \frac{e^{x} - (1/e)^{x}}{2} \to \infty\).
Jab \(x \to -\infty\), to \(e^{x} \to 0\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x} \to \infty\). Is liye \(\sinh x = \frac{e^{x} - (1/e)^{x}}{2} \to -\infty\).
Natija: \(\sinh x\) ki range \(\mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(e^{-x}\) ko \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}\) kyun likha? Taa ke dono hisse section 1.4 wale exponential functions \(a^{x}\) ban jayein: \(e^{x}\) ka base \(e > 1\) hai (barhta hua function) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}\) ka base \(\frac{1}{e} < 1\) hai (ghatta hua function). In dono ka \(\pm\infty\) par rawaiya (behaviour) humein pehle se maloom hai, us se \(\sinh x\) ka rawaiya mil jata hai.
Range poora \(\mathbb{R}\) kyun? \(\sinh x\) continuous hai (graph mein koi toot nahin), baayen taraf \(-\infty\) tak neeche jata hai aur daayen taraf \(\infty\) tak upar. Raaste mein woh har real value se guzarta hai. Saath hi yeh strictly increasing hai (barhta hua \(e^{x}\) minus ghatta hua \(e^{-x}\) hamesha barhta hai), is liye har value sirf ek dafa milti hai. Isi wajah se \(\sinh x\) ka inverse mumkin hai (page 1.5.4).
\(x = 0\) par \(\sinh 0 = \frac{e^{0} - e^{-0}}{2} = \frac{1 - 1}{2} = 0\), is liye \(\sinh x\) ka graph point \((0, 0)\), yani origin se guzarta hai.

Ab values ka table. Har value calculator se nikli hai; misaal ke taur par \(\sinh 2 = \frac{e^{2} - e^{-2}}{2} \approx \frac{7.389 - 0.135}{2} \approx 3.63\). Kitab ke table mein \(x = 3\) wali value ghalat chhapi hai, is liye hum sahi value likh rahe hain (neeche box dekhiye):

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab ke table aur Figure 1.8 mein \(\sinh 3\) ki value 10.03 (aur \(\sinh(-3)\) ki \(-10.03\)) chhapi hai. Sahi value yeh hai:
\[\sinh 3 = \dfrac{e^{3} - e^{-3}}{2}\]
\[\approx \dfrac{20.0855 - 0.0498}{2}\]
\[\approx 10.0179 \approx 10.02\]
Yani sahi entries 10.02 aur \(-10.02\) hain. (Ise \(\cosh 3 \approx 10.07\) se mat milaiye.) Hamari figure mein 10.02 hi plot kiya gaya hai.
In points ko jor kar \(\sinh x\) ka graph Figure 1.8 mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = sinh x on axes from x = minus 3 to 3 and y = minus 12 to 12. The curve rises from bottom left to top right through the origin, with plotted points (minus 3, minus 10.02), (minus 2, minus 3.63), (minus 1, minus 1.18), (0, 0), (1, 1.18), (2, 3.63) and (3, 10.02).
blocks.caption: Figure 1.8: the graph of y = sinh x (original drawing after the textbook's figure; sinh 3 plotted as 10.02)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table mein ek khoobsurat baat dekhiye: \(\sinh(-x) = -\sinh x\). Yani \(-1, -2, -3\) wali values, \(1, 2, 3\) wali values ki bilkul negative hain. Aise function ko odd function kehte hain, aur us ka graph origin ke gird symmetric hota hai: Figure 1.8 ko ulta (\(180^{\circ}\) ghuma kar) dekhein to bilkul waisa hi lagega.
Saboot: \(\sinh(-x) = \frac{e^{-x} - e^{x}}{2} = -\frac{e^{x} - e^{-x}}{2} = -\sinh x\). Is ka faida: aap sirf positive \(x\) ki values nikalein, negative wali khud mil jayengi.
(ii) Graph of cosh x

Ab bilkul isi tareeqe se \(\cosh x\) dekhte hain. Hum jaante hain ke \(\cosh x = \frac{e^{x}+e^{-x}}{2}\), jise is tarah likh sakte hain:
\[\cosh x = \dfrac{e^{x} + \frac{1}{e^{x}}}{2} = \dfrac{e^{x} + \left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}}{2}\]
Kyun ke \(e^{x}\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x}\) ka domain \(\mathbb{R}\) hai, is liye \(\cosh x\) ka domain bhi \(\mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\) hai.

Jab \(x \to \infty\), to \(e^{x} \to \infty\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x} \to 0\); is liye \(\cosh x = \frac{e^{x} + (1/e)^{x}}{2} \to \infty\).
Jab \(x \to -\infty\), to \(e^{x} \to 0\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^{x} \to \infty\); is liye \(\cosh x = \frac{e^{x} + (1/e)^{x}}{2} \to \infty\).
Farq dekhiye: \(\sinh\) mein minus tha is liye ek taraf \(-\infty\) gaya; \(\cosh\) mein plus hai, is liye dono taraf \(\infty\) ki taraf jata hai.

\(x = 0\) par \(\cosh 0 = \frac{e^{0} + e^{-0}}{2} = \frac{1 + 1}{2} = 1\). Is liye \(\cosh x\) ka graph point \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai aur \(y = 1\) graph ki sab se kam (minimum) value hai. Natija: \(\cosh x\) ki range \([1, \infty)\) hai. Graph banane ke liye hum values ka table lete hain:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
1 hi sab se choti value kyun hai? Ek pakki baat: kisi bhi real number ka square kabhi negative nahin hota.
\[\left(e^{x/2} - e^{-x/2}\right)^{2} \ge 0\]
\[e^{x} - 2 + e^{-x} \ge 0\]
\[\dfrac{e^{x} + e^{-x}}{2} \ge 1\]
Yani har \(x\) ke liye \(\cosh x \ge 1\), aur barabar sirf tab jab \(e^{x/2} = e^{-x/2}\), yani \(x = 0\). Dono kinaare \(\infty\) ki taraf jate hain, is liye range bilkul \([1, \infty)\) hai.
In points se \(\cosh x\) ka graph Figure 1.9 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Shakal "U" jaisi hai, bilkul latakti hui zanjeer ki tarah.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = cosh x on axes from x = minus 4 to 4 and y = 0 to 11. A U-shaped curve with lowest point (0, 1), symmetric about the y-axis, through (plus or minus 1, 1.54), (plus or minus 2, 3.76) and (plus or minus 3, 10.07).
blocks.caption: Figure 1.9: the graph of y = cosh x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan table batata hai ke \(\cosh(-x) = \cosh x\): dono taraf ek jaisi values. Aise function ko even function kehte hain, aur us ka graph \(y\)-axis ke gird symmetric hota hai (Figure 1.9 ko \(y\)-axis par mor dein to dono hisse ek doosre par aa jayenge). Saboot: \(\cosh(-x) = \frac{e^{-x} + e^{x}}{2} = \cosh x\).
Kyun ke 1 se upar har height do dafa aati hai (ek dafa \(x\) par aur ek dafa \(-x\) par), is liye \(\cosh x\) poore \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one nahin. Isi liye us ke inverse ke liye domain ko mehdood (restrict) karna parega (page 1.5.4).
Dono graphs ka muqabla ek table mein:

blocks.caption: sinh x aur cosh x aamne saamne
rows: Odd: \(\sinh(-x) = -\sinh x\), origin ke gird symmetric
\((-\infty, 0]\) par ghatta, \([0, \infty)\) par barhta; one-to-one nahin

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Imtihan mein graph banane ka qadam ba qadam tareeqa (dono functions ke liye):
1. Pehle axes kheenchiye aur scale tay kijiye. \(\sinh\) aur \(\cosh\) ki values tezi se barhti hain (\(x = 3\) par taqreeban 10), is liye \(y\)-axis par 2, 4, 6 ke qadam lena behtar hai.
2. Khaas point lagaiye: \(\sinh\) ke liye \((0, 0)\), \(\cosh\) ke liye \((0, 1)\).
3. Table ki values se \(x = 1, 2, 3\) ke points lagaiye, aur symmetry se negative \(x\) wale points: \(\sinh\) mein sign badal kar, \(\cosh\) mein wahi value.
4. Points ko haath se smooth curve se joriye, seedhi lakeeron se nahin, aur kinaaron par teer (arrow) lagaiye taa ke pata chale ke graph aage bhi jaari hai.
5. Aakhir mein curve ka naam likhiye, jaise \(y = \sinh x\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cosh\) ke graph ka neecha hissa \((0, 1)\) par gol (rounded) hota hai, nukeela (V jaisa) nahin.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Figure 1.8 aur 1.9 ko saath rakhiye. Bare \(x\) (jaise \(x = 3\)) par \(\sinh x\) aur \(\cosh x\) ki values (10.02 aur 10.07) bohat qareeb kyun hain? Socha? Bare \(x\) par \(e^{-x}\) taqreeban zero ho jata hai, to dono taqreeban \(\frac{e^{x}}{2}\) ban jate hain. Dono ka farq bilkul \(e^{-x}\) hai: \(\cosh x - \sinh x = e^{-x}\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: (Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai.) \(\cosh x\) aur parabola \(y = x^{2} + 1\) dono \((0, 1)\) se shuru hote hain aur U-shape hain. Kya dono ek hi hain? \(x = 5\) rakh kar dekhiye: \(\cosh 5 \approx 74.2\), jab ke \(5^{2} + 1 = 26\). Yani \(\cosh x\) exponential hai aur parabola se kahin tez barhta hai. Graph banate waqt \(\cosh\) ko kabhi parabola na samjhiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\sinh x\): domain aur range \(\mathbb{R}\), \((0, 0)\) se guzarta hai, odd hai, hamesha barhta hai (one-to-one).
2. \(\cosh x\): domain \(\mathbb{R}\), range \([1, \infty)\), sab se neecha point \((0, 1)\), even hai, \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one nahin.
3. Kinaaron ka rawaiya \(e^{x}\) aur \(e^{-x}\) se aata hai: \(x \to \infty\) par \(e^{x} \to \infty\), \(e^{-x} \to 0\), aur \(x \to -\infty\) par is ka ulta.
4. Table: \(\sinh 1 \approx 1.18\), \(\sinh 2 \approx 3.63\), \(\sinh 3 \approx 10.02\); \(\cosh 1 \approx 1.54\), \(\cosh 2 \approx 3.76\), \(\cosh 3 \approx 10.07\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\cosh x\) ka graph origin se guzaarna: yeh \((0, 1)\) se shuru hota hai, kyun ke \(e^{0} + e^{0} = 2\) aur \(2/2 = 1\).
2. \(\cosh x\) ko parabola \(y = x^{2} + 1\) samajhna: 0 ke qareeb milte julte hain magar \(\cosh x\) bohat tez barhta hai.
3. \(\sinh x\) ka koi minimum ya maximum bana dena: is ka koi nahin; yeh barhta hi rehta hai.
4. \(\cosh x\) ki range \((1, \infty)\) likhna: \(x = 0\) par value bilkul 1 hai, is liye bracket band (closed) hai: \([1, \infty)\).
